text:
Ravi: heads-up: linkcheck failed on the staging deploy for /guides/perf-tuning.md — fragment `#cache-keying` not found but the heading is definitely there locally.
Laura: ugh we've seen ghost fragments like this before. Can you paste the exact heading? invisible chars sometimes sneak in from copy/paste.
Ravi: sure — copied from the source file:
```
### Cache keyingand invalidation

We recommend prefixing requests...
```
LinkCheckerBot: linkcheck error: page=guides/perf-tuning.md fragment=cache-keying status=404 run=CI#15022
Ollie: I see a NUL (\u0000) between words — that'll change the slug generation. How did that get in there? maybe from a Windows editor or a bad snippet paste.
Laura: nice catch. Two fast options: 1) remove the invisible char from the heading, 2) add an explicit id: `### Cache keying and invalidation {#cache-keying}`
Ravi: I'll remove the stray char and push a tiny PR. Also adding the explicit id as a defensive step.
DocsInfra: consider adding a pre-commit hook to strip non-printable/control chars from markdown. We already run prettier-md; we can add a sanitize step.
Ollie: also add a docs linter rule that flags headings with control/unicode-categories=Cc. That would have caught this at author time.
Ravi: small PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4522 — removed \u0000 and added explicit id. Local linkcheck passes.
LinkCheckerBot: CI queued for PR #4522
Laura: while we're here, can we canonicalize heading slugs across mkdocs/docusaurus by adding a short section in CONTRIBUTING about explicit ids for headings with punctuation/unicode? saves churn.
DocsInfra: OK I'll open a follow-up to add a sanitize hook and update CONTRIBUTING. Ticket DOCS-515 created.
LinkCheckerBot: CI passed for PR #4522  All checks green.
Ollie: LGTM, merged. Thanks Ravi for the quick fix.
Ravi: thanks everyone 389 Closing thread — will follow up on the sanitize hook in DOCS-515.
